p2 Savaṃta: name normalized to stem 'Savanta'; role 'reader' removed (paṭhanārthaṃ only makes him the person the copy was made for, so beneficiary); confidence medium

relations.evidence: bhāṇejasavaṃta (bhāṇeja = sister's son, presumably of the scribe)

purpose: for the study of the scribe's nephew (bhāṇeja) Savanta (paṭhanārthaṃ)
notes: The era is written only as 'samvat'. VS is assumed from the Devanagari script, the north-Indian setting and the catalogue field, giving 1644 CE (Śrāvaṇa śukla 12, a Sunday); the weekday was not checked. 'vārāsāsyāṃ' is most likely a corrupt 'vārāṇasyāṃ' (Vārāṇasī). The passage 'vyākhyā vālakṣilyājñātitrā' is corrupt: 'vyākhyā' may stand for the surname/title 'vyāsa', and 'vālakṣilyājñāti' probably means 'of the Vālakhilya caste (jñāti)'; 'trā' may be a fragment of a further title (e.g. Trivāḍī/Trivedī). 'bhāṇeja' (Hindi/Rajasthani) means sister's son. The name Savaṃta (Savanta/Sāvanta) is uncertain. The final phrase 'śrī lakṣmī nṛsiṃyojati' is a corrupt benediction 'śrīlakṣmīnṛsiṃho jayati'; it names a deity, not a person.
